body:
Found in the review of PR #2323 (issue #2317). None of these items gives wrong output today.

1. `crates/motion/src/machining2d/arc_touch.rs:82-90`: with one NaN end, the NaN guard at line 86 does not fire. Non-finite chords are not sent there today. Add an explicit finite check at the start of `grazes`.
2. `arc_touch.rs:58`: the reach calculation skips a NaN bracket point, so a touch could be made from such a bracket. The bracket code does not make one today. Refuse a bracket with a non-finite point.
3. The `TOUCH` bound (1e-5 mm) is pinned only by the two `arc_touch` unit tests. Add an end-to-end fixture: a chord 1e-3 mm inside the end tangent of a corner arc must be a crossing in the emitted pocket.
4. `docs/decisions/2317-blend-crossing-law.md` says "the unrounded pass" for the fallback after 3 rounds. Some fitted arcs stay chords there. Correct the wording.

Done means: items 1 to 3 have tests that fail without the change, and item 4 is corrected.

title: main is red (post-merge gate): the data_dir lookup does not know the new cargo build-dir layout

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P2

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## Run

Post-merge gate run 43990986558 (`post-merge.yml`, batch tier, self-hosted Linux runner) on `3f41b8da6b65b8154132878e459d4430e3fb2063` ended `failure`. 199 test binaries report `test result: FAILED` in the `gate-logs` artifact.

## Cause

PR #2293 (`e2ca9443b`) reads posts and machine files from disk at run time (`crates/post/src/data_dir.rs`). The dev candidates (`<profile>/../../assets`, `<manifest>/../../assets`) apply only when `cargo_profile_dir` finds the cargo build tree. It finds the tree only by the old cargo layout:

- the exe folder is `target/<profile>` or `target/<profile>/{deps,examples}`;
- that profile folder holds `.fingerprint`.

The cargo of the runner uses the new build-dir layout. Test executables are in `target/debug/build/<pkg>/<hash>/out/`, not in `target/debug/deps/`. Fingerprints are in each unit folder, so `target/debug/.fingerprint` does not exist. Thus `cargo_profile_dir` returns `None`, and the lookup tries only `<exe dir>/assets/<kind>`.

Evidence from the artifact logs:

```
     Running unittests src/lib.rs (target/debug/build/camcraft-post/4d4a6b2fbedf41a7/out/camcraft_post-4d4a6b2fbedf41a7)
thread 'data_dir::tests::the_dev_run_finds_the_repository_assets' panicked at crates/post/src/data_dir_tests.rs:123:52:
no posts folder found - the program needs its assets/posts directory beside the executable (looked in: /home/ghrunner/runner-work/Camcraft/Camcraft/target/debug/build/camcraft-post/4d4a6b2fbedf41a7/out/assets/posts)
```

Each "looked in" list in the logs has one path only (hash replaced by `H`, count of lines):

```
    424 .../target/debug/build/camcraft-app/H/out/assets/posts
    213 .../target/debug/build/camcraft-app/H/out/assets/machines
     15 .../target/debug/build/camcraft-ui/H/out/assets/machines
     11 .../target/debug/build/camcraft-ui/H/out/assets/posts
      4 .../target/debug/assets/posts          (camcraft-cli, the uplifted binary)
      1 .../target/debug/build/camcraft-post/H/out/assets/posts
```

The last-but-one line shows that the uplifted `target/debug/camcraft-cli` also fails. Thus `target/debug/.fingerprint` is absent in this layout, and a dev run (`cargo run`) with this cargo also fails.

Windows worktrees pass because the local cargo (1.99.0) uses the old layout.

## Grouped failures

1. Lookup (most binaries): the panic text or the refusal names `no posts folder found` or `no machines folder found`. Examples: `post` lib, `shipped_from_disk`, `logging`, `wcs_index`, `rigid_tapping`, `mcp_live`, `lathe_work_spindle`, `ui` lib, `ui` `machine`.
2. Lookup, shown as a different assertion: tests that compare against a shipped machine or post. Examples: `control_comp` and `wear_comp` goldens (the program has `(CAMCRAFT)` and no `M8`, because the default machine is not read), `lathe_workholding_live`, `ui` `machine_mode_tests` and `gate_route_tests`.
3. Not yet explained: `camcraft-motion` `corner_arc_radius` (`Waterline: no corner turned on an arc`). The motion crate does not read posts. The fix of this issue examines it on Windows and reports.

## Done means

- `cargo_profile_dir` accepts the old and the new cargo layout, for test executables and for the uplifted binaries.
- An installed exe without its `assets/<kind>` folder is still refused by name.
- A unit test pins the new layout and fails without the fix.
- The next post-merge run shows no `no posts folder found` and no `no machines folder found`.

title: A stock-source 2D Chamfer into a part added after generation posts when the program sim judges the stock

labels.name: bug

labels.name: P1

body:
A stock-source 2D Chamfer can post a cut into a part. This occurs when the part is added after generation and the program sim judges the stock.

## Reproduction

The fixture of `crates/app/tests/stock_source_holes.rs` (`stock_source_chamfer_refusal_names_cause_and_part_as_source_workaround`, the "chamfer-rejudge-hint" case):

1. Use `job(Model::hole(3.0, 8.0), HALF, rotated)` with `HALF = 35`.
2. Generate a stock-source 2D Chamfer, `chamfer(1.0)`. The generation is clean.
3. Import a part "other": a plate on x [30, 35], y [-5, 5], z [0, 20].
4. Call `posting::post_setup`.

Result on `main` at `7e26134bf`:

- Stock aligned: `POSTED`. The program has `G01 X35. Y-35. Z19.` along the edge of "other".
- Stock turned a quarter about Z: `POSTED` (the red case of #2306).
- Stock turned 1e-6 rad about Z (the sim does not judge): `post blocked - ... S1 now cuts part 'other' (move 5 cuts past the finish surface (stock-source chamfer breaks into a part; ...`.

## Cause

In `crates/app/src/posting_sim.rs`, `judge_clause` calls `kept_moved` (the live re-judge of #1628, `operation::kept_rejudge::moved_part_problem`) only in the `Err(reason)` arm, when the sim does not judge. In the `Ok(_)` arm with zero gouge cells, the re-judge does not run. The column sim does not see this chamfer cut into "other". Thus the post goes out.

- The aligned case exists since #1628 (commit `329db7d80`).
- #2182 (#2177) made the sim judge a quarter-turned box. Thus the quarter-turned case now also posts.

## Proposed fix

Run `kept_moved` also in the `Ok(_)` arm when the sim finds no gouge. Add a pinning test for the aligned and the quarter-turned stock. Then run each suite that posts, because the change can add refusals.

Found during #2306.

title: Post: a generic LinuxCNC mill post (3-axis), separate from the Tormach PathPilot post

labels.name: enhancement

labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
### What are you trying to do

I run a 3-axis mill on LinuxCNC 2.9 (Remora controller, `M6` remapped to an automatic tool changer) and would like to post from CamCraft straight to it. There is no plain LinuxCNC post today. The Tormach PathPilot post is the closest, but it carries Tormach assumptions, so its output has to be checked and hand-edited before it is safe on a stock LinuxCNC machine. #435 / #495 is one example: the retract assumed machine Z0 is the top of travel.

### How you imagine it working

A generic LinuxCNC mill post (e.g. `linuxcnc.cps` plus a `linuxcnc-3axis.mch` machine), written to the RS274NGC dialect as LinuxCNC documents it, with no PathPilot-specific codes. LinuxCNC machines differ a lot from one another, so the machine-specific parts would be options rather than fixed:

- **Retract and tool-change position:** `G53 G0 Z<value>` with a user value (machine Z0 is not always the top of travel), `G28`/`G30`, or none.
- **Tool change:** `T<n> M6` then `G43 H<n>`, with an option to leave out `G43` when the `M6` remap applies the tool length itself.
- **Path blending:** `G64 P<tolerance>` with a user value, or `G61` exact path.
- **Program start/end:** a safe block (`G17 G90 G40 G49 G80`, units, work offset); end with `M5 M9` and `M2` or `M30`; optional `%` delimiters.
- **Drilling and tapping:** `G81`/`G82`/`G83`/`G73`. LinuxCNC's rigid tap is `G33.1`, which needs a spindle encoder, so an option to refuse or expand taps on a machine without one.
- **Arcs:** `G2`/`G3` with incremental IJK (LinuxCNC's default `G91.1`), helices allowed.
- Comments in parentheses, no line numbers by default; spindle `M3`/`M4 S`, coolant `M7`/`M8`/`M9`.

Happy to run posted programs through a LinuxCNC 2.9 sim and air-cut them on my machine, and report back.

body:
Maintainer, 2026-11-16: "Issue, Bug, P2, mch, cps, themes, scripts - should be read from disk at runtme and not dompiled into the binary."

What happens: the build compiles these data files into the executable with `include_bytes!` / `include_str!`. Known places:

- the post processor scripts (`assets/posts/*.cps`), in `crates/app/src/posting.rs` (54 includes);
- the machine files (`.mch`);
- the themes;
- the scripts.

A user cannot change, add or replace one of these files without a new build. An executable without an `assets` directory beside it shows all of them.

Expected: the application reads these files from disk at run time.

Work:

- List each `include_bytes!` / `include_str!` of a machine file, a post script, a theme or a script in `crates/*/src`. Icons, the application icon and fonts are not in the scope of this issue.
- Define one data directory lookup (beside the executable first, then the per-user data directory) in one module. Each reader uses it.
- Read the files at start or on first use, and cache the result. Do not read a file per frame.
- A missing or malformed file gives a clear error that names the file and the directory. It does not crash. A post script that fails to load refuses the post by name.
- Each release package ships the directories (see PR #2044, which ships `examples`). Packaging script and workflow changes need the maintainer's decision: name them in the PR body.
- The browser build has no disk. Keep the compiled-in copy for the `wasm32` target only, and say so.
- Tests read the files from the repository `assets` directory.

Safety: a post script read from disk can be edited by a user, and it then changes the posted G-code. Show the path of the loaded post script in the post dialog or the program header comment, so that a user can see which file made the program. The verify check and the post gate do not change.

Open design questions (the worker records its choice in `docs/decisions/`):

- Whether a compiled-in copy stays as a fallback on desktop when the directory is missing. The maintainer's words say no.
- The order of the lookup when the same file name is in two directories.

Done means: the desktop executable holds no compiled-in machine file, post script, theme or script. A test pins that an edited file on disk changes what the application loads. A test pins the error for a missing directory. The packages of a cut hold the directories.

What happens:

- Project `testdata/models/fig8.camproj` (model `fig8.step`), 2D Adaptive, tool `EM-0800-4FL` (8 mm end mill), post Fanuc (built-in).
- Lead in / Lead out page: Entry Type `Helix`, Helix radius 1.6 mm, Minimum radius, pitch and angle on Auto, Plunge enabled.

Expected:

- Each entry into material uses the selected entry type (helix), at each region and each level.
- Where the helix does not fit, the ramp comes next. A straight plunge into material is the last fallback only.
- Each entry that falls back gets a warning that names the region, the level and the reason. The page says "where the helix cannot fit, a ramp and then a plunge stand in": the user must see when this happens.

body:
The maintainer reported this in chat on 2026-11-15, on v0.21.0, with a screenshot of a 2D Adaptive operation.

His words: "a common issue i see is that the first toolpath is always ontop of the part at TopZ ... even thos stepdown states "full depth" of the cut.. technically it should just be one single toolpath right?" and "find it in all operations.. This is a high effortf, P2 bug.."

## What happens

The operation has Top Z = 13 (stock top + 1), Bottom Z = 0 and Stepdown = 50 mm. It posts two full levels: one at Z 13 and one at Z 0. The level at Top Z cuts no material. It doubles the cycle time of a one-level cut.

## Cause

The shared level law starts its list at Top Z:

```rust
// crates/motion/src/machining2d/levels.rs, cut_levels
let mut z = top;
while z > bottom + tol {
    zs.push(z);      // the first level is `top`
    z -= stepdown;
}
zs.push(bottom);
```

`cut_levels(13, 0, 50)` gives `[13, 0]`. The correct list is `[0]`. With a stepdown of 5 it gives `[13, 8, 3, 0]`. The correct list is `[8, 3, 0]`.

`crates/app/src/operation/area.rs` `ladder_planes` restates the same law, and its unit test pins the wrong list (`ladder_planes(20.0, 0.0, 5.0) == [20, 15, 10, 5, 0]`).

## Callers found (read-only search, not complete)

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/`: `adaptive_troch.rs:158`, `bore.rs:308`, `circular.rs:278` and `:280`, `contour_params.rs:216` (2D Contour), `face.rs:156`, `pocket.rs:277`, `pocket_hsm.rs:49` and `pocket_troch.rs:68` (level counts for the budget), `slots.rs:160` and `:343`, `trochoid_slot.rs:319`
- `crates/motion/src/machining3d/entry.rs:89`, `:123`, `:236`, `:258` (3D Pocket and its rest pass)
- `crates/app/src/operation/area.rs:74`, `:182`, `:233` (`ladder_planes`, the 3D pocket region build)
- `crates/motion/tests/control_comp.rs` (a test helper with the same name)

Not yet read: `crates/motion/src/finishing3d/ladder.rs` `levels`, `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_depth.rs` `ladder`, `crates/motion/src/machining3d/ladder.rs`, the turning, drilling (peck), engraving, chamfer, plasma and EDM depth ladders, and each operation with its own loop.

## For the work

1. Audit each operation of each machine type for a level at Top Z (or at the material top) that removes no material. List each in the PR with the result.
2. Fix the shared law so that the first level is `top - stepdown`, and the last level is `bottom` exactly. Use one law: `ladder_planes` in `app` must use the motion law, or match it by a shared test.
3. Check the special cases:
   - Top Z below the stock top (material above Top Z): no level may cut more than one stepdown. Find what each operation means by Top Z, and state it.
   - `circular.rs:278` starts at a previous level (`cut_levels(prev, floor, ...)`): make sure that it does not cut the previous level two times.
   - Face: a single pass at `cut_z` stays one pass.
   - A stepdown of 0 or a span of 0: the current refusal and the one-plane result stay.
   - Rest machining and the 3D Pocket shell levels: the level count and the budget readings change. Restate the budget pins with the reason.
   - The ramp, helix and plunge entries that read `top_z` as the material top (`Motion::top_z`) must stay correct.
4. The size of the last step (the remainder or equal steps) is a separate choice. Keep the current remainder rule, and file a follow-up issue for the choice.

This changes posted G-code for existing projects (one level fewer for each depth-stepping operation). It is under the safety floor.

## Done means

- No operation posts a level at Top Z that removes no material when Top Z is at or above the material top.
- One-level case: Top Z 13, Bottom Z 0, Stepdown 50 gives one level at Z 0. Pinned for 2D Adaptive, 2D Pocket, 2D Contour, Slot, Bore, Circular and 3D Pocket.
- Multi-level case: Top Z 20, Bottom Z 0, Stepdown 5 gives `[15, 10, 5, 0]`. Pinned on the shared law and on `ladder_planes`.
- Each changed golden is listed in the PR with the reason. The PR says that posted G-code changes.
- Each verify and gouge pin of the touched operations stays green.

body:
Add a clean-room Mach4 milling postprocessor (`assets/posts/mach4.cps`) specced solely from public Mach4 and RS-274/NGC documentation.

### Context
- `assets/posts/` and `BUILTINS` in `crates/app/src/posting.rs` contain no Mach4 or MachMotion post today.
- Standard Mach4 lacks `G43.4` RTCP, supports `G93` inverse-time feed (`F` on every feed block) and `G94`, limits `G2/G3` arcs to Cartesian planes (`G17/G18/G19`), uses `G43 H..`, `G53`/`G28`/`G30` safe retracts, and `G64` constant velocity mode.
- Depends on machine schema (#1962), AC IK solver (#1965), and `G93` timing (#1966).

### Requirements
- Author `assets/posts/mach4.cps` from public Mach4 Mill GCode Programming documentation only (Clean-Room Protocol). Register it in `BUILTINS` (`crates/app/src/posting.rs`).
- Leave 3-axis programs in standard `G94` mode with `G2/G3` arcs unchanged.
- Handle 3+2 indexed sections by retracting safely in `G94`, positioning `G0 A.. C..` (with optional unclamp/clamp M-codes), and cutting in `G94` with rotated planar coordinates and arcs.
- Handle simultaneous 5-axis sections by outputting no `G43.4`, linearizing arcs to `G1`, switching to `G93`, emitting pre-compensated `X Y Z A C` and `F` on every `G1` block, and restoring `G94` after the section.
- Respect Mach4 rotary rollover settings (`unwrapped` vs `rollover_360` option) and unwind safely only at retract `Z`.
- Refuse tilted/simultaneous posting by name if the machine lacks required trunnion geometry or states `controller.rtcp = true` unexpectedly without matching setup.

Done means: `mach4.cps` posts valid Mach4 G-code for 3-axis, 3+2 indexed, and simultaneous 5-axis sections in mm and inch, refuses missing trunnion geometry by name, and passes golden conformance tests.

title: Lathe post stream: state the stock's turning radius, so a box stock's rotating corners are inside the G30 envelope

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

body:
Found while fixing #1604.

**What happens:** the post stream states the stock only as its axis-aligned box (`StockXYLeft/Right/Front/Back`, `StockZTop`). The fix for #1604 in `assets/posts/tormach-lathe.cps` uses the largest half-width of that box as the stock's radius about the spindle axis. That is exact for a round bar. A box stock (a square bar) turned on a lathe sweeps a circle of half its diagonal, so its rotating corners stand outside the radius the post uses. The departure before G30 (`+X` to the stock's diameter) and the approach after G30 can then pass inside the corners' circle.

**Why the post cannot fix it alone:** the stream does not say if the stock is a round bar or a box. Half the diagonal for every stock puts every turning start "inside" a round bar (a start at Ø12.1 on a Ø12 bar is inside Ø16.97), so every turning program would be refused.

**Expected:** the stream states the stock's turning radius about the work-offset Z axis (for example a `StockTurnRadius` PARAM from `post::dump`, the swept radius of the stock shape), and `tormach-lathe.cps` (and `fanuc-lathe.cps` where it applies) uses it in place of the box's half-width.

**Workaround:** use a round-bar (cylinder) stock for lathe setups.

**Done means:** a lathe stream states the stock's turning radius; the Tormach lathe post's G30 approach and departure use it; a pin with a square-bar stock shows no G30-adjacent rapid inside the corners' circle.

body:
Part of #1446 (first slice: the motion-crate generator, `camcraft_motion::machining2d::rest_plan` / `rest_pocket`, on branch `issue/1446-rest-2d`).

Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, quoted on #1446): "We wanna cover some of the toolpaths and things like that at first." and "Lets create issues on your suggestions, they made sense." Sources as he asked: "We should use perplexity to find literature on those types of toolpaths and not copy them straight up".

What the first slice leaves out of the generator, each of which needs design before code:

1. **2D Adaptive over a rest area.** `rest_pocket` refuses the Adaptive strategy by name. The adaptive plan picks its own entry and bounds engagement assuming a full pocket; over a rest area the entry should stand in cleared floor and the engagement model must know what is already cut.
2. **Entry from already-cut space.** The first slice plunges into each rest area like a plain pocket, so nothing depends on the cleared-area estimate. Entering sideways from cleared floor is faster, and makes that estimate safety-critical: the cleared area must be read small (it is today) and the entry refused, by name, where it cannot be proved.
3. **The previous tool from the previous operations.** Today the previous tool is entered by hand and trusted (the path says so in a note). The issue also asks for "from previous operations": the cleared area measured from the stock the earlier operations of the setup leave, including their depth - a rest pass must not assume a depth the roughing never reached. Where the carried stock cannot be established, refuse by name or mark incomplete; never guess.
4. **Zigzag.** Refused by name in the first slice because rows leave cusps along the walls of a rest area. A row plan with a closing ring per rest area would lift the refusal.

Literature to start from (cited in the first slice): Held, "On the Computational Geometry of Pocket Machining", LNCS 500, 1991; Veeramani and Gau, Computer-Aided Design 29(12), 1997, and IIE Transactions 32, 2000; Yao, Gupta and Nau, Computer-Aided Design 35(9), 2003. No code or text from any other CAM product (Clean-Room Protocol).

Done means: each of the four is either built with its pinning tests (verifier clean, no rapid into material the cleared-area reading cannot prove cut, refusals named) or split into its own issue with a recorded decision; the literature used is cited in the PR.

Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat), after a feature comparison with the open-source project stevecad/camlib: "We wanna cover some of the toolpaths and things like that at first." and, on the suggested picks: "Lets create issues on your suggestions, they made sense." On sources: "We should use perplexity to find literature on those types of toolpaths and not copy them straight up".

What is missing: hole making has drilling and tapping cycles only. There is no reaming, boring, fine boring or dwell-at-depth cycle, and no spot-face / counterbore dwell. The tool kinds (reamer, spot drill, countersink, centre drill) are open issue 897; this issue is the cycles and their posted output.

Wanted, as cycle choices on the drilling operation (a user parameter with a default, never hard-wired):
- Reaming: feed in, feed out (G85 where the post has it, expanded moves otherwise).
- Boring: feed in, spindle stop, rapid out (G86); feed in, dwell, feed out (G89).
- Fine boring: feed in, oriented spindle stop, shift off the wall, rapid out (G76 on a mill), with the shift amount and direction as parameters. A post or machine with no spindle orientation refuses it by name rather than posting a retract that drags the tip up the wall.
- Dwell at depth for spot facing and counterboring (G82), in the unit each post expects.

Safety: every post either writes the cycle correctly for its dialect, expands it to plain moves, or refuses by name. A dwell is never silently dropped or written in the wrong unit (seconds against milliseconds). The canned cycle and its expanded form remove the same stock in simulation.

Sources: RS-274 / ISO 6983 and each control maker's published programming manual for the cycle words, found by a literature search (Perplexity) at the start of the work and cited in the PR. camlib is a feature list only: no code is copied or adapted from it.

Done means: each cycle generates, simulates and posts on Fanuc, Haas, Heidenhain, Sinumerik, grblHAL and PathPilot as a canned cycle, an expansion or a named refusal, pinned by a golden per post; an MCP parameter for the cycle choice; a fine bore on a machine without spindle orientation is refused in a test. Not exercised on real controls unless the PR says otherwise.

body:
Maintainer direction (2026-11-11): "We should aim for a high cohesion low coupling thru out our codebase as we are built crates and tests. And every gate is very costly."

Where the cost comes from today (measured 2026-11-11 on main 0e36fd14):

| Crate | Source lines | Test files (one binary each) | Depends on (workspace) |
|---|---|---|---|
| app | 72,122 | 267 | cl, geometry, motion, post, sim, tools |
| ui | 57,060 | 14 | app |
| motion | 46,643 | 65 | cl, geometry, sim, tools |
| sim | 23,444 | 50 | cl, geometry, tools |
| post | 6,181 | 5 | cl, geometry |
| geometry | 5,539 | 4 | - |
| tools | 4,306 | 1 | - |
| cl | 3,723 | 1 | - |
| kernel | 1,185 | 5 | - |

- `app` is the hub: it depends on every domain crate, so almost any change rebuilds it, and each of its 267 test files links the whole crate into its own binary.
- Tests of one domain's behaviour live in `app` (post dialect tests such as `fanuc_post`, `tormach_post`, `heidenhain_*` sit in `crates/app/tests/` while `crates/post/tests/` has 5 files), so a post-only change still builds and links `app`.
- A geometry / cl / Cargo change falls back to the batch tier.
- Each worktree's `target/` is 25-56 GB; five builds at once took the disk from 166 GB to 13 GB free on 2026-11-11.

Open questions to answer here (research, no code):
1. Fan-out: for a change in each crate, which crates and how many test binaries rebuild and relink, and how long does it take (cold and warm, with #913's cache)? One table.
2. Test placement: which `crates/app/tests/*` files test behaviour owned by post, sim, motion, cl, tools or geometry and could move to that crate with a small fixture seam instead of the whole app? Count per target crate.
3. Test binaries: what does folding a crate's test files into a few binaries (one per gate-map group) save in link time and disk, and what does it cost (`gate test <name>` selection, parallel runs, the quick tier's changed-test picking in `xtask/src/plan.rs`)?
4. Coupling: which `app` modules could become their own crate (the M4.1 seams still inside `app`: operation, project, commands, mcp, machine), and which dependencies between domain crates could be cut or inverted (motion -> sim; the new post -> tools from PR #880)?
5. Rules: which of this becomes law in AGENTS.md "Code shape" and a reviewer check (e.g. a test lives in the crate that owns the behaviour; a new dependency between workspace crates needs a decision entry; no new test file in `app` for behaviour another crate owns)?

Then file the concrete sub-issues (each with P*, effort, area, "Done means", "Part of #<this>"), ordered by gate minutes saved per unit of work, and close this umbrella.

Related: #900 / PR #913 (compile cache and lighter dev profile), #27 (kernel seam).

title: Process changes - fork maintainers please subscribe

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

body:
**Subscribe to this issue** (the "Subscribe" button on the right) if you work from a fork of CamCraft, especially with an AI agent.

Forks sync product code only at release tags (AGENTS.md "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag"). But the *process* - `AGENTS.md`, the agent definitions in `.claude/agents/`, the skills in `.claude/skills/` and `scripts/gate.*` - changes between releases, and a fork's agents should follow the current rules (review labels, priority labels, release steps, and so on).

**How it works:**
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one number. Every PR that changes a process file bumps it.
- Every such PR also adds a comment **here**: the new version, what changed, and what to pull. Subscribers get one notification per change.
- A fork's agent compares its `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with upstream's at the start of each session and, if upstream is newer, pulls just the process files (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session"). Product code still waits for the next release tag.

**To pull by hand:**
```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh
git commit -m "chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>"
```

This issue stays open and pinned. It's labelled `P?` so no agent ever picks it up as work.
